I ask because myself and others keep gaslighting one another over what’s latest and what isn’t There's a breakout call today to talk about the EIP. After that it might change again: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1118 > I think you meant PER_EMPTY_ACCOUNT_COST * effective_gas_price It seems common for EIPs to drop `effective_gas_price` multiplier when discussing gas costs as it is implied when discussing that unit. I can make it clearer we're discussing gas though > Authorizations are not rolled back for aborted transaction, so abort in this case also wouldn't roll back previous authorizations in the list (I guess it's fine or at least consistent) This makes sense to me since there is nothing conditional about an authorization. If it is included, it's included. Only the execution can be conditional > This changes the guarantee that valid transactions will not fail with not enough sender balance - i.e. extra balance check is required when transferring value could you expand on this? i don't think i understand this might address some of your concerns https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/8775 thanks, charging it as intrinsic cost and refunding is less awkward way, yes cool thx for the feedback this still needs to be changed/clarified I think 100 gas is for storage no? i think the warm account read is rolled into CALL* family? account access too EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODECOPY, EXTCODEHASH and CALLs all charge 100 if warm, 2600 if cold in 7702 they should be 100 or 2600 [+ 100 or 2600] ah you're right, i will update it dumb Q: how does current 7702 support sponsorship if the EOA needs to actually deploy the tx type? The EOA only needs to sign the autorization, not the tx. The tx sponsor includes the signed authorization into a 7702 transaction and sends it.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content:
> I think you meant PER_EMPTY_ACCOUNT_COST * effective_gas_price
It seems common for EIPs to drop `effective_gas_price` multiplier when discussing gas costs as it is implied when discussing that unit. I can make it clearer we're discussing gas though

> Authorizations are not rolled back for aborted transaction, so abort in this case also wouldn't roll back previous authorizations in the list (I guess it's fine or at least consistent)
This makes sense to me since there is nothing conditional about an authorization. If it is included, it's included. Only the execution can be conditional

> This changes the guarantee that valid transactions will not fail with not enough sender balance - i.e. extra balance check is required when transferring value
could you expand on this? i don't think i understand
